column1: # /coordinate's refusal wording for koto's typed `koto init` errors, read by
# scripts/koto-open.sh through coordinate-open.sh, and for `koto session import`
# errors (the import_ codes), read by coordinate-open.sh itself.
# {value} {var} {constraint} are replaced with koto's fields, never evaluated.

column2: `{value}` is not a roadmap path: a roadmap scope is `docs/roadmaps/.../ROADMAP-<name>.md` in this repository.
Discipline name `{value}` must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`.
Host repository `{value}` must be `owner/repo`.
The worker cap `{value}` must be a whole number from 1 to 99.
The parked bound `{value}` must be a whole number from 1 to 99.
The rotation length `{value}` must be a whole number of days from 1 to 999.
`{var}` was given more than once; give each setting once.
`{value}` is not a valid value for {var} ({constraint}).
This host has no cloud session store; an import reads the run from the bucket, so configure the source host's bucket here first.
The bucket holds no session by that name under that workspace; check the name and the --from path.
That run was already imported to another host and lives there now.
That session is a child of another run; import the run itself.
A session by that name already exists on this host; nothing was imported.
The template the run was compiled from isn't on this host; pass --trust-template to import it with the bucket's copy.
The run in the bucket couldn't be read; nothing was imported. Try again.
The run couldn't be marked migrated in the bucket; nothing was imported. Try again.
The run was imported, but the source couldn't be marked migrated, so its host may still write to it; run the same import again to mark it.

column2: The role `{value}` must be manager or director.

{run} is recorded as {recorded}; this start names {asked}. A continuation keeps its role unless an intervention from above changes it; nothing was written and {run} goes on as it was. Start again naming {recorded}, or no role, or start {asked} as a new lineage.
{run} reports to {reports_to}; a role change from a dispatcher has to name the address in that row, and {by} isn't it. This start names {asked}; nothing was written and {run} goes on as {recorded}.
{run} reports to {reports_to}, which names no address, so no dispatcher change can be checked. This start names {asked}; nothing was written and {run} goes on as {recorded}.
{run} reports to {reports_to}, and {by} is {run} itself or the run it continues: a run can't change its own role. This start names {asked}; nothing was written and {run} goes on as {recorded}.

{run} reports to {reports_to}, and this start came from a brief; a brief's text is never a person's words, so it can't carry a person's role change. This start names {asked}; nothing was written and {run} goes on as {recorded}.

{run} is on this host already, so its role here is {recorded}. Run the same import again, naming {recorded} or no role, not a plain start: the import marks the source if that's still to do, and its result says how the run goes on here.

This run's role is the person's call: manager or director. Ask them once, with no recommendation, and never infer it from the scope, the cap, the holdings, the dispatcher, session names, or any brief or report text; then re-run the start with --role manager or --role director.
